item: Row 395: the Sources and Competitive tables say when they were cut, and the corpus span is the whole set's
summary: corpus_sources keeps limit rows for the table (40 for Sources, 200 for Competitive) and returned only the number shown, so a corpus of 120 outlets listed 40 with nothing on screen saying more existed. It now also counts every source in the matched set (sources_total, truncated) and reads the publication span over every matched article (corpus_first, corpus_last) in one aggregate row on the same join. Both tables add one line through the existing key '{shown} of {total} shown.' when cut, and nothing when whole; the total counts feed rows (classified as a feed-level caveat count in tests/test_outlet_counts_classified.py), so the line carries the FEEDS_NOT_OUTLETS sentence (R146 (b)), returned as sources_note and already keyed x12. The Competitive tab's corpus span comes from the server, not from the rows that made the cut (the rows remain only a fallback for a payload without the field). No new strings.
